guideTitle: 5 Best Plastic-Free Food Storage Containers in 2026
metaDescription: Compare five plastic-free food storage containers in glass and stainless steel, with lid materials, oven limits and microwave rules explained for buyers.
introParagraphs: Plastic-free food storage sounds simple until you start reading listings. A glass body with a plastic snap lid is not plastic-free, a silicone gasket is a different material from a rigid plastic lid, and some containers marketed as plant-based are still molded resins. The five sets below were chosen because the listing describes glass, glass lids, silicone or stainless steel as the food-contact materials, rather than leaning on a BPA-free label alone.

We evaluated each set on lid construction, heat limits, size range and how realistic it is to live with day to day. Glass bases are the common thread, but the lids split the group: borosilicate versus semi-tempered glass, silicone-framed versus bamboo-framed, and one stainless steel bento-style set that avoids glass weight entirely. Those lid choices decide whether you can reheat in a microwave, leave the lid on, or put it in a dishwasher.

This is a shopping guide based on product specs and listing details, not a lab report, so wherever a listing is silent on something like oven temperature or dishwasher use, we say to check the product page instead of guessing.

products.name: Ziruma Glass Food Containers, 4-Pack
products.description:
The Ziruma set is described as plastic and BPA free, with a glass body and a glass lid, and the listing stresses airtight lids that keep contaminants out. The 35 oz size equals 4.4 cups, which is large enough for a portioned dinner or a batch of soup without feeling oversized in a fridge shelf. Because the lid is glass as well, there is no rigid plastic part touching the food at any point in the system.

The tradeoff is weight and fragility, which is true of every glass set but matters more with a generous 35 oz volume. A full container of stew is noticeably heavy to carry, so this is a home-fridge and meal-prep choice more than a commute lunch choice. The listing family also includes a 21 oz version and a multi-size version, so buyers who want smaller portions should open the right variant instead of assuming the large size fits every need.

In ownership terms, the straight glass lid is easy to wash and has fewer crevices than a gasketed snap lid, but check the product page for how the airtight seal is formed and whether the lid is rated for the microwave or dishwasher. Compared with the Urban Green round set, which uses a silicone-framed vented lid, the Ziruma lid is a simpler glass-only design. Against the VERDESSA set at 27 oz, the Ziruma gives you roughly 8 oz more room per container. If you want the most capacity per piece in this lineup, this is the one to start with.
products.bestFor: Home cooks who want large glass containers with glass lids for batch cooking and leftovers.

products.name: Everusely Stainless Steel Food Containers, Set of 5
products.description:
Everusely takes a different route from glass: premium-grade stainless steel with food-grade silicone, with no plastic named in the materials. The set covers five sizes from 3 oz up to 32 oz (about 100 ml to 950 ml), which is the widest size spread among our picks. That range lets one set handle sauces, snacks, sides and a main dish in the same lunch bag.

The obvious limitation is that steel is opaque, so you cannot see leftovers without opening the lid, and it is not a microwave container. Anyone who reheats at a desk will need to move food to a plate first, and the listing does not make claims about oven or dishwasher use, so confirm on the product page. The steel body, however, will not crack when dropped in a bag or shatter in a sink the way glass can.

Day to day, this is the lightest option to carry in the lineup compared with a glass container of the same volume, and the 32 oz piece is about the same size as the VERDESSA 27 oz glass base. The tiny 3 oz and 6 oz pieces have no equivalent in the Ziruma or Urban Green sets, which stick to larger meal-prep volumes. If your goal is packed lunches or school and work bags, this is the best match here, while a home fridge full of reheated leftovers is better served by glass.
products.bestFor: Packed lunches and portable meals where breakage matters more than microwave use.
pros: Stainless steel and silicone, no plastic stated
Five sizes from 3 oz to 32 oz
Will not shatter if dropped
Bento-style compartments suit lunches

products.name: Urban Green Round Glass Meal Prep Containers
specs: Microwave safe lid on, vent open
products.description:
Urban Green builds the lid from semi-tempered glass framed in silicone, and the listing says the lid contains only glass and premium silicone with no plastic. The round version has a leak-proof lid with an air vent, so steam can escape when you heat food. The listing says it is microwave safe with the lid on, as long as the vent is left open.

That vent instruction matters. A sealed lid in a microwave builds pressure, and the maker explicitly tells owners to open the vent, which is a small habit to form but an easy one to forget. Semi-tempered glass is also not the same as borosilicate, so rapid temperature swings deserve more caution than the listing language implies; check the product page for oven guidance.

Round containers waste a bit of rectangular fridge space but are easier to clean in the corners and to stir in the microwave. Compared with the Urban Green rectangle set, the round design trades stacking efficiency for easier cleaning and more even reheating of soups and grains. Against the Ziruma set, the vent gives it a clear edge for microwave reheating with the lid in place. Anyone reheating most meals will appreciate the vented lid more than the extra capacity of larger sets.
products.bestFor: People who reheat soups, grains and leftovers often and want the lid to stay on.

Vent lets steam escape while heating
Leak-proof lid described by the maker

cons: Vent must be opened before microwaving

products.name: Urban Green Rectangle Glass Containers, 3-Pack
products.description:
This is the rectangular sibling of the round Urban Green set, sold as a 3-pack with the same silicone-framed glass lid. The listing repeats the main claims: every piece is plastic free, the lid has an air vent, and it is microwave safe with the lid on as long as the vent stays open. Rectangles stack and nest neatly, so three of them take up less fridge or cabinet space than three rounds of the same volume.

Three containers is a smaller commitment than a four-piece set, which suits one or two people who prep a few meals at a time but may leave you short for a full week of lunches. Capacity per piece is not stated in the part of the listing we reviewed, so open the product page before ordering if your portions are large. As with the round set, the maker recommends leaving the vent open while heating.

In use, a rectangular container fits sandwiches, fish fillets and flat grains better than a round one, and it slides into a lunch bag more easily. Compared with the Urban Green round set, you gain stacking efficiency but lose some ease of stirring in the corners. Against VERDESSA, the Urban Green lids close with a silicone frame and vent while the VERDESSA bamboo lid is non-locking, so this is the better match for carrying food without spills.
products.bestFor: Small households that want stackable rectangular glass with a vented lid.
pros: Plastic-free glass and silicone construction
Rectangle shape stacks and nests tightly
Vented lid for microwave reheating
Leak-proof lid described by the maker
cons: Only three pieces in the pack

products.name: VERDESSA Glass Containers with Bamboo Rim, 4-Pack
products.description:
VERDESSA pairs a high-borosilicate glass base with a lid that has a glass center and a natural bamboo frame. The listing says the base is oven safe up to 450°F and also microwave safe, which makes it the most oven-friendly container in this plastic-free group. Borosilicate handles temperature changes better than ordinary glass, so it is the one to pick if you want to bake or roast and then store in the same dish.

The lid is where the tradeoffs live. It is a non-locking, secure-fitting design rather than an airtight snap lid, so we would not trust it for carrying soup in a bag. The listing also says to hand wash the lid only, while the glass base is dishwasher safe, so cleaning is a two-step routine.

The 27 oz size sits between the Ziruma 35 oz and the smaller Everusely pieces, which fits a single serving of casserole or a pasta bake. Compared with Urban Green, the VERDESSA lid is nicer on a counter but less spill-proof, and the lid cannot go in the dishwasher. If you cook in the oven often and mostly store in the fridge, this is the better choice, while commuters should lean toward Urban Green or Everusely.

buyingCriteria.explanation: A glass base does not make a set plastic-free, because lids, gaskets and latches are often rigid plastic. Look for a listing that names the lid material, not just the body. In this lineup, the Ziruma has a glass lid, the Urban Green sets use semi-tempered glass framed in silicone, and the VERDESSA uses glass with a bamboo frame. The Everusely avoids glass altogether and names stainless steel with food-grade silicone.

Borosilicate glass handles thermal shock better than ordinary glass, so it is safer to move from fridge to oven or microwave. Only the VERDESSA base names high-borosilicate and gives a 450°F oven limit. The Urban Green lids are described as semi-tempered glass, which is a reminder to avoid sudden temperature swings and read the product page for limits. As a rule, never put a cold glass container straight into a hot oven unless the listing allows it.

The lid is the weak point of any container, so decide whether you need an airtight seal or just a cover. The Ziruma lists airtight glass lids and the Urban Green lists leak-proof vented lids, while the VERDESSA is explicitly non-locking and secure-fitting. A non-locking lid is fine for a fridge shelf but poor for a lunch bag. If you carry food, choose a locking or silicone-sealed design, and check whether the gasket can be removed for cleaning.

A tight lid on hot food builds steam pressure, which is why vented lids exist. The Urban Green listing says the lid is microwave safe only with the air vent left open, and that instruction is easy to miss. Make the habit of opening the vent before pressing start, and stop if you hear popping. The Everusely steel set cannot go in a microwave at all, so plan to move food to a plate.

buyingCriteria.criterion: Size range matters more than count
buyingCriteria.explanation: A pack of four same-size containers sounds like value, but the wrong size gets left in the cabinet. The Ziruma 35 oz suits a full dinner, the VERDESSA 27 oz suits a single casserole serving, and the Everusely set runs from 3 oz to 32 oz. If you store sauces and snacks, small pieces matter, and only the Everusely covers that range. For batch cooking, aim for at least two containers per large recipe.

Glass is heavy and can chip, so consider where the container will travel. A full 35 oz glass piece is a lot to carry on a commute, while a 32 oz steel piece from Everusely weighs far less empty. At home, the heft is rarely a problem, but an older buyer with limited grip may find large glass awkward. If carrying is the main use, steel or smaller glass sizes are safer picks.

howWeEvaluated.title: Material transparency
howWeEvaluated.description: We read each listing for what the body, lid and seal are made of and gave credit only for materials the maker named. Ziruma, Urban Green and VERDESSA name glass lids or glass-and-silicone or bamboo frames, and Everusely names steel and silicone. Listings that only said BPA free were treated as incomplete. A plastic-free claim needs to cover the lid.

howWeEvaluated.title: Heat handling
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared stated microwave and oven limits. The VERDESSA base is the only one with a named oven ceiling of 450°F, while the Urban Green lids are microwave safe with the vent open. The Everusely set gives no microwave route, so it was judged as a cold-storage and lunch set. Anything not stated was marked as unknown.

howWeEvaluated.title: Lid design and carrying
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at whether the lid locks, vents or simply sits on top. The Ziruma and Urban Green lids are described as airtight or leak proof, while the VERDESSA is non-locking. That makes Urban Green and Ziruma better for transport, and VERDESSA better for fridge storage and serving.

howWeEvaluated.title: Size range and usability
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared capacities, from the Everusely 3 oz to 32 oz range to the Ziruma 35 oz and VERDESSA 27 oz pieces. A wider range scored better for varied use, and a large single size scored better for batch cooking. Pack counts of three or four were considered against a typical week of meals.

howWeEvaluated.title: Cleaning and ownership
howWeEvaluated.description: We considered dishwasher notes, hand-wash lids and crevices. The VERDESSA base is dishwasher safe but its lid is hand wash only, which adds a step. Glass lids without gaskets, like the Ziruma, have fewer places to trap residue. Ownership favors the simplest lid that still seals.

cards.label: Glass
cards.text: Glass is transparent and can usually go in a microwave, so you can see and heat food in one container. The picks here are Ziruma, Urban Green round and rectangle, and VERDESSA. The downside is weight and breakage. Pick glass if you mostly reheat at home.

cards.label: Stainless Steel
cards.text: Steel will not shatter, weighs less and survives bags and drops, but it is opaque and not microwavable. The pick is Everusely, with sizes from 3 oz to 32 oz. Pick steel if you carry lunches and eat food cold or reheat on a plate.

faq.q: Which of these is best if I want zero plastic?
faq.a: Everusely is the cleanest on paper because the listing names stainless steel and silicone with no plastics. Among glass sets, the Urban Green listing says every piece is plastic free, and the Ziruma lists a glass body and glass lid. Always check the product page for gaskets and any plastic latch.

faq.q: Can I microwave glass containers with the lid on?
faq.a: Only if the maker says so. The Urban Green listing says its lid is microwave safe with the lid on, provided the air vent is left open. Without a vent, steam builds pressure, so remove or open the lid in any other case. The Everusely steel set should not be microwaved at all.

faq.q: Is borosilicate really better than regular glass?
faq.a: Borosilicate resists thermal shock better, which matters when moving between fridge, oven and microwave. The VERDESSA base is the one pick that names high-borosilicate and gives a 450°F oven limit. Other sets do not state this, so treat them more cautiously and avoid sudden temperature changes.

faq.q: Is a bamboo lid food safe and durable?
faq.a: The VERDESSA lid has a glass center in a natural bamboo frame, and the maker says to hand wash the lid only. Wood and bamboo can crack or warp if soaked or run through a dishwasher. Keep it out of the microwave and dry it promptly.

faq.q: Why do my glass lids not seal well?
faq.a: Seals depend on lid design. The VERDESSA lid is non-locking, so it is not meant to be leakproof, while airtight and silicone-framed lids fit tighter. Also check that the gasket is clean and seated, because food residue can break the seal.

faq.q: Which size should I buy for meal prep?
faq.a: Match the container to your portion. The Ziruma 35 oz holds a large dinner, the VERDESSA at 27 oz fits a single casserole serving, and the Everusely covers 3 oz sauces to 32 oz mains. If you are unsure, choose a set with at least two sizes or buy two small sets.

faq.q: Are glass containers safe for the freezer?
faq.a: The listings we reviewed do not all say. Glass can crack if you fill it to the brim and freeze, because liquids expand. Leave headspace, let hot food cool first, and check the product page before freezing.
